introduction: These hundred readings come from a world in which letters and numbers were read as signs. The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh speak of the Point from which all letters unfold, of the mysteries of Alif and Bá, of the number nine, of names reckoned by the values of their letters, and of the science called jafr; many passages are prayers and visionary praise in that idiom. The later readings turn the matter around: questions about numerology and divination are set aside, and the questioner is told that today the greatest thing is to save one who is drowning. Other scriptures use the same language, from Alpha and Omega and the number of the beast to the letters that open chapters of the Qur’an, and Pythagoras thought number the element of all things. Beside these stand the warnings: against divination, against calculating the end, against fables and endless questions, and for the plain sense.
questions: The readings find worlds hidden in a point and a letter. What do you make of the long human habit of finding meaning in the letters of sacred words?
Humpty Dumpty says a word means what he chooses. What keeps a symbolic interpretation honest?
A promise is attached here to the year nine, and Daniel counts days; Newton and the Talmud both warn against calculating. How do you weigh prophecy by numbers?
Deuteronomy forbids divination and Isaiah mocks the stargazers. Where is the line between seeking hidden wisdom and trying to control the future?
Paul says the letter kills and the spirit gives life. How does that bear on a science of letters?
The last readings set numerology aside in favour of saving one who is drowning. What speculative interests of your own might need the same reordering?

outside.why: Jesus drew a lesson from the same small bird: not one sparrow falls without the Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
Emerson wrote that every natural fact is a symbol of some spiritual fact.
William Blake wrote of seeing a world in a grain of sand, and holding infinity in the palm of the hand.
In the Book of Revelation God is named by the first and last letters of the alphabet: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending.
John's Gospel begins: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.
The Qur’an says that if the sea were ink for the words of the Lord, the sea would be used up before His words were exhausted.
Aristotle reports that the Pythagoreans supposed the elements of numbers to be the elements of all things, and the whole heaven to be a musical scale and a number.
The Tao Te Ching counts creation out: the Tao produced One, One produced Two, Two produced Three, Three produced all things.
The Qur’an says in a single short verse: We have created every thing by measure.
Lewis Carroll's Humpty Dumpty says of a word: it means just what I choose it to mean. How is a symbolic reading of letters and numbers kept from meaning whatever the reader chooses?
The second chapter of the Qur’an opens with three letters, Alif, Lam, Mim, before a word is said.
John's Gospel says that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.
Proverbs promises understanding of a proverb and its interpretation, the words of the wise and their dark sayings.
The psalm says that by the word of the Lord were the heavens made.
In Genesis God said, Let there be light, and there was light.
The Letter to the Hebrews says that the worlds were framed by the word of God.
Juliet asks what is in a name, since a rose by any other name would smell as sweet. Is the meaning of a name in its letters or in the one who bears it?
Emily Dickinson answers those who say a word is dead when it is said: I say it just begins to live that day.
The Qur’an says that His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says unto it: Be! and it is.
Wittgenstein wrote that the limits of my language mean the limits of my world. What can be said about the letters of a creating word in the letters of our own?
Hillel put the entire Torah into one sentence, and said the rest is its interpretation.
Ben Bag Bag said of the Torah: turn it over, and again turn it over, for all is therein.
Another chapter of the Qur’an begins with a single letter and an oath: Nun. By the pen and that which they write.
The Qur’an says that God taught Adam all the names, and then showed them to the angels.
Genesis says that whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.
Plato's Socrates concludes that a name is an instrument of teaching and of distinguishing natures.
The prayer Jesus taught begins: Our Father which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name.

The Qur’an says that some of its verses are clear and are the substance of the Book, and others allegorical, and warns of those who pursue the allegorical. Where does devout study of hidden meanings turn into what this verse warns against?
The psalmist says: the entrance of Thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
Thomas Aquinas held that all the senses of scripture are founded on the literal, from which alone any argument can be drawn. What can a meaning found in letters and numbers prove?
The seer of Revelation saw one who had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.
The Book of Revelation invites the same reckoning of a name by its letters: let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast.
Proverbs says that it is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
Irenaeus argued in the second century that the Gospels could be neither more nor fewer in number than they are. What kind of reasoning is an argument from the fitness of a number?
When Moses asked the name, God said: I AM THAT I AM.
Genesis counts the days of creation and says that on the seventh day God ended His work.
Asked how often to forgive, Jesus answered with a number that is not meant to be counted: until seventy times seven.
The Book of Daniel reckons the future in numbers: seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city.
The risen Jesus told his disciples: it is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in His own power. How should a promise attached to a numbered year be held?
The Talmud speaks harshly of those who calculate the end of days, since people lose hope when the date passes. What is the risk in prophecy by numbers, even when a date proves true?
Habakkuk is told that the vision is yet for an appointed time: though it tarry, wait for it.
Isaiah speaks of a vision become as the words of a book that is sealed, which neither the learned nor the unlearned can read.
Proverbs says that the name of the Lord is a strong tower; the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
The Book of Daniel ends with numbers of days, a thousand two hundred and ninety, and a blessing on him that waiteth.
Isaac Newton wrote that the folly of interpreters has been to foretell times and things by prophecy, as if God designed to make them prophets. What is numerical prophecy for, if not prediction?
Moses says: the secret things belong unto the Lord our God, but those things which are revealed belong unto us.
Daniel is told to shut up the words and seal the book, even to the time of the end.

John's Gospel records that the net held a hundred and fifty and three great fishes, a number readers have puzzled over ever since. When does a number in a sacred text carry a meaning, and when is it only a count?
Emerson wrote that language is fossil poetry, each word once a brilliant picture.
The Chandogya Upanishad says that the differences among things are only a name, arising from speech.
The priestly blessing asks: the Lord make His face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee.
Paul says: the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. How does that saying apply to a science of letters?
Genesis begins with the heaven and the earth created, and the Spirit of God moving upon the face of the waters.
The Qur’an says that the Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
In Genesis God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night.
The Tao Te Ching says that the name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
Isaiah asks: to whom then will ye liken God, or what likeness will ye compare unto Him?
The psalm says that God telleth the number of the stars; He calleth them all by their names.
Through Jeremiah God says that if a nation turn, He will repent of what He had pronounced concerning it.
Jesus used the same title of himself: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.
Montaigne remarked that there is more ado to interpret interpretations than to interpret things. How much commentary can a symbol bear?
Emerson wrote that the eye is the first circle, the horizon the second, and that this figure is the highest emblem in the cipher of the world.
The Preacher says: one generation passeth away, and another generation cometh, but the earth abideth for ever.
Deuteronomy forbids any one that useth divination, or an observer of times. How is a science of letters to be told apart from what the Torah forbids?
Isaiah says: lift up your eyes on high, and behold who bringeth out their host by number.
The psalm asks: so teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
Job says to God: for now Thou numberest my steps; dost Thou not watch over my sin?
Leibniz held that each simple substance expresses all the others, and is a perpetual living mirror of the universe.
Whitman, shown the proofs and figures in columns, went out and looked up in perfect silence at the stars. What does counting capture of a creation made through numbers, and what escapes it?
Asked in effect when his end would be, Hamlet says: if it be not now, yet it will come; the readiness is all.
The psalmist asks: whither shall I go from Thy spirit? If I ascend up into heaven, Thou art there.
A verse of the Qur’an reads in full: above it are nineteen. What does a bare number in scripture invite a reader to do?
Thomas Aquinas wrote that it is not unfitting if, even according to the literal sense, one word in Holy Writ should have several senses.
The psalmist says: I will praise Thee, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Paul asks: know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost?
Matthew's Gospel ends: lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.
Jesus told his disciples: it is expedient for you that I go away.
The psalm says: not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Thy name give glory.
Israel's daily confession begins: hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord.
In Isaiah God says: I am God, declaring the end from the beginning.

When two disciples wished to call down fire on a village that would not receive him, Jesus rebuked them: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. How should prayers for the destruction of unbelievers be read?
Jesus taught: love your enemies, bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you. What becomes of a prayer against the faithless in the light of this command?
The psalms too ask for judgment: Lord, how long shall the wicked triumph?
The psalmist prays: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
Daniel read the words on the wall as numbered, weighed and divided: Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin.
Isaiah mocks a city's astrologers, stargazers and monthly prognosticators: let them stand up and save thee. Why have the prophets so often distrusted those who read the future from signs?
Plato held that rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul.
The first letter of John says: let us not love in word, neither in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
Jesus said that not every one that saith Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom, but he that doeth the will of the Father.
In the parable a Samaritan, when he saw the wounded man, had compassion on him and went to him.
The first letter to Timothy says: neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions rather than godly edifying.
The Letter to Titus says: avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, for they are unprofitable and vain.
Shakespeare's Edmund calls it the excellent foppery of the world that we make guilty of our disasters the sun, the moon, and the stars.
Jesus said to Martha: thou art careful and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful.
Paul says: I had rather speak five words with my understanding than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.
Jesus distinguished the tithing of mint and cummin from the weightier matters of the law.
Francis Bacon wrote that human knowledge and human power meet in one.
Micah asks what the Lord requires but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.
Sir Thomas Browne read his divinity in two books, the written one of God and the universal manuscript of nature.
The Preacher says that he counted one by one to find out the account, which his soul sought and he found not. What place should curiosity about hidden correspondences have in a religious life?

matthew-one-jot-or-one-tittle.text: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled

psalm-telleth-the-number-of-the-stars.text: He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names. Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite

deuteronomy-useth-divination.text: There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch. Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord

acts-times-or-the-seasons.text: It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power

timothy-fables-and-endless-genealogies.text: Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do. Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned

john-hundred-and-fifty-and-three.text: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken

job-numberest-my-steps.text: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin

ecclesiastes-counting-one-by-one.text: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found

titus-avoid-foolish-questions.text: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain

corinthians-five-words-with-my-understan.text: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue

quran-alif-lam-mim.text: Alif. Lam. Mim. This is the Scripture whereof there is no doubt, a guidance unto those who ward off (evil)
